what_worked: Clear investor-audience framing with a three-pick recommendation structure gives the deck a usable shape.
fix_next: Almost no actual dataset analysis is shown—replace marketing copy with charts, distributions, and verifiable findings from the 1,000-row dataset.
verdict: A pitch deck for TrustMRR, not a data-story from the dataset.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '$1.5B+ in total verified revenue' — dataset total 30-day revenue is ~$15.6M, not $1.5B. Slide 3: '78% of cases revenue outpaced follower growth' — no follower data in dataset, claim unverifiable/fabricated. Slide 3: '$10K–100K MRR tier represents highest-density zone' — 67.7% are $0–1K, so $0–1K is highest density; the claim contradicts their own chart. Slide 8: '67.7% Revenue-Positive' mislabeled — 67.7% is the $0–1K tier share, not the share that is revenue-positive (784/1000 = 78.4% have >$0 revenue). Slide 2: '$1.2B+ in verified startup revenues across 53M transactions' — not derivable from dataset and likely fabricated platform marketing.

evidence.insight: No original analysis of the dataset. Picks (Stan, Conductor, AI Website Builder) appear sourced from the TrustMRR website, not from systematic data exploration. No distributions, correlations, category comparisons, or provider analysis.
evidence.narrative: Has a coherent arc (overview → picks → recommendation) but it is a sales pitch for TrustMRR acquisitions, not a data-driven story. Slides 4, 9, 10 are generic consulting frameworks with no data backing.
evidence.framing: Audience (investor) is stated, but the assignment was a data-story presentation, not a marketing pitch. No mention of dataset scope (1,000 rows), missingness, or limitations. No definitions of metrics used.
evidence.accuracy: Total revenue inflated ~100x ($15.6M → $1.5B). The 78% follower-growth claim has no basis in the dataset. The 67.7% figure is reused with a wrong label. MRR tier percentages are plausible but unverified. No charts derived from actual data.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme via Gamma template. Legible text, decent hierarchy. But decorative AI illustrations dominate; only one donut chart exists and it lacks axis/source labels. Slides 9–10 are pure stock-illustration filler.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy Gamma AI template usage: decorative illustrations on every slide, consulting-style numbered frameworks (slides 4, 9, 10), inflated language ('structural tailwinds', 'category dominance'), and no real data visualizations. Slide 10 is entirely generic post-acquisition advice applicable to any company.
